content:
Rumors suggest Apple's fall iPhone lineup this year will center around the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra. Here are the three most important feature differences (excluding price) that could influence your upgrade decision.

Design: Traditional vs. Foldable

This difference is the most obvious, but it's still worth highlighting, as it's also the most crucial point.

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will continue the fundamental design that has defined the iPhone for years. Reports indicate the screen size and overall design will be identical to the previous generation. If you prefer the feel of a traditional iPhone, the iPhone 18 Pro will be your top choice.

As for the iPhone Ultra, it will be Apple's first foldable model. Its design is entirely different—the outer screen is shorter and wider than a traditional iPhone, while the inner screen resembles an iPad mini.

Camera: Pro Still Tops the Class

Apple has consistently poured its most cutting-edge and innovative camera technology into the Pro lineup. This year is no exception.

The iPhone Ultra is expected to offer nearly identical camera capabilities as the iPhone 18 Pro, with one major exception: it won't feature a telephoto lens.

Sources indicate the iPhone Ultra will use the same main lens, ultrawide lens, and front-facing camera as the Pro series. However, the telephoto lens remains exclusive to the Pro lineup, with performance expected to improve further this year.

Performance: Both Feature the A20 Pro Chip, But Materials Differ

Both the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra are expected to come equipped with the A20 Pro chip. However, due to differences in design and materials, actual performance may vary.

The iPhone 18 Pro will retain the same aluminum unibody design as the iPhone 17 Pro, along with the same vapor chamber cooling system. These two changes resulted in significantly improved overall performance for the iPhone 17 Pro compared to its predecessor, as the iPhone can maintain lower temperatures under heavy loads.

As for the iPhone Ultra, it will adopt a lightweight titanium design similar to the iPhone Air. It may also feature a vapor chamber, but currently only one source has made this claim. However, due to the different materials, even with the same chip as the iPhone 18 Pro, the iPhone Ultra may still fall slightly short in performance under direct sunlight or when running demanding tasks.
